lanes.name: Kick
lanes.txt: Kick on 1, 2, 3 and 4. Four to the floor: the 909 kick has a hard attack that cuts through a club system.

lanes.name: Clap
lanes.txt: Clap on 2 and 4, the backbeat. The 909 clap is analog: a burst of filtered noise, triggered several times in a row.

lanes.name: Closed hat
lanes.txt: Closed hat on the 16ths, with a gap on every 'and'. On the 909 the hats are 6-bit samples, not analog circuits.

lanes.name: Open hat
lanes.txt: Open hat on every off-beat, the 'and'. A closed hat chokes it, so the two lines share the bar.

lanes.name: Kick
lanes.txt: Kick on every beat. The 808 kick is a sine wave with a long Decay knob: turn it up and it becomes a boom.

lanes.name: Clap
lanes.txt: Clap on 2 and 4, plus one on the 'a' of 4. That last 16th pushes the loop back to the 1.

lanes.name: Closed hat
lanes.txt: Closed hat on the 8ths, straight. Thin and metallic: six square-wave oscillators mixed together.

lanes.name: Cowbell
lanes.txt: Cowbell on the 'and' of 1, the 'a' of 2, the 'and' of 3 and the 'e' of 4. Two square waves, detuned.

lanes.name: Kick
lanes.txt: A plain four-to-the-floor kick to hold the floor. The 303 has no drums: it is a bass synth with a 16-step sequencer.

lanes.name: 303 notes
lanes.txt: One note per step. The 303 stores pitch and rhythm in two separate passes, which makes programming it famously awkward.

lanes.name: Accent
lanes.txt: Accent: the note is louder and the filter opens wider. This is where the squelch comes from.

lanes.name: Slide
lanes.txt: Slide: the note glides into the next one and the gate stays open. No retrigger, just a bend.
